name: Fair comparison: equal protection for every forecast
approved: design_review.md, approved by the project owner with: raw errors primary and centred errors as sensitivity; bias-corrected point plan added; ExtraTrees-24 point plans may differ from the checkpoint by up to 1e-6 beds, the other four must match exactly; the 0.95 level is indicative only
problem: a point forecast that runs high gets free insurance under a cost that punishes shortfalls ten times more than spare beds; every method therefore gets the same deliberate protection, built from its own past errors

data.blanks: months with a blank value are dropped
data.cutoff_rule: rows after a cut-off are discarded before any value is converted

forecasts.common: each method forecasts occupied and available separately, six months ahead, from the 24-month training window only
forecasts.Persistence: last month of the window, flat
forecasts.Seasonal naive: same calendar month one year earlier

SARIMA-24.target_scaling: StandardScaler fitted on the 24 window values; forecasts inverse-transformed

ExtraTrees-24.feature_rule: lags and shifted rolling mean/std (ddof 1) of the target, plus calendar values
ExtraTrees-24.training_rows: rows whose features need data before the window are dropped (12 rows expected)
ExtraTrees-24.forecasting: recursive, six steps, earlier predictions feed later features
ExtraTrees-24.note: the project pipeline's median imputer is a no-op here because no feature is missing

reuse: scripts/clean_checkpoint/pipeline.py imported unedited: load, forecast_origin, lp_plan, cost_table, rank_origin, overall

error_bank.backtest_origins: every month b whose 24-month window starts at or after the first data month and with b + 6 months <= the planning origin
error_bank.procedure: at each b refit all five methods on the 24 months ending at b with the unchanged specification and forecast six months
error_bank.error: actual - forecast for occupied and available; gap error = occupied error / 0.90 - available error; one six-month path per backtest
error_bank.non_convergence: if SARIMA-24 does not converge at b, b is dropped for all methods at that origin and logged; stop below 20 paths

scenarios.primary: gap forecast path of the method plus each of its own raw error paths; equal weights
scenarios.sensitivity: the same with errors centred per horizon
scenarios.quantile: level q for month t: the ceil((n + 1) q)-th smallest scenario gap (the largest if the rank exceeds n)

plans.point: LP on the point forecast (reference, no protection); at p = 5,000 it is the clean-checkpoint LP plan
plans.bias_corrected: LP on the point forecast plus the mean error path (reference: bias removed, no margin), p = 5,000
plans.protected: PRIMARY. SAA: one shared plan (x, a, r) minimising the average over scenarios of running, opening, closing and shortfall cost, same limits, p = 5,000
plans.penalty_sweep: point and protected plans at p = 1,000, 2,500 and 10,000; each planned and scored at its own p with its own hindsight
plans.service_level: minimise operating cost subject to x_t >= the (1 - alpha) quantile of the scenario gaps (not below zero), alpha = 0.10 and 0.05; if the ramp or the cap makes it unreachable the requirement is lowered to the reachable level and logged; scored with operating cost, short months, shortfall bed-months and cost at p = 5,000
plans.hindsight: the LP on the actual gaps, for each p
plans.tie_break: inside the SAA program 0.0001 is added to the running cost per bed-month so that equally cheap plans resolve to the smaller one; reported costs never include it

measures: gap MAE and mean signed gap error (actual - forecast) of the point forecast
pinball loss at 0.9 of the 0.9 quantile forecast (beds), and of the point forecast as a reference
coverage: months with the actual gap at or below the 0.9 quantile, of 6 per origin and of 12 pooled
CRPS of the scenario set; pinball loss at 0.5, 0.8 and 0.95
error bank summary: paths, mean and standard deviation of the gap error, average margin (0.9 quantile - point forecast)
per plan: operating cost, shortfall bed-months, short months, shortfall cost, total, excess over hindsight

rules.primary_endpoint: realised cost of the protected plan at p = 5,000; five plans per origin
per_origin: tie band for cost: 1% of that origin's hindsight cost
tie band for pinball loss and MAE: 5 beds
rank the five protected plans by realised cost; plans within the tie band of the cheapest are 'joint best'
across_origins: overall ranking: combined excess over hindsight

'clear winner': a method whose protected plan is joint best at both origins, or that beats the overall runner-up by more than the tie band at each origin; otherwise 'no clear winner' with the joint-best methods; if more than one method meets the definition all are reported as joint winners

previous winner: at each origin the method with the cheapest point plan; it 'still wins' if its protected plan is joint best at that origin, otherwise it 'no longer wins'; its protected rank is reported
did protection help: point cost - protected cost per method and origin; 'helped' above the tie band, 'hurt' below minus the tie band, otherwise 'no material difference'
best-calibrated forecast: lowest mean pinball loss at 0.9 across both origins; 'clear' only if lowest at both origins by more than 5 beds; coverage is reported without a rule
robust to the penalty: the clear-winner rule is applied at each p; the base result is 'robust' if the outcome (the same winner, or 'no clear winner') is the same at all four levels
service level: no winner is declared
improvement_measures: value of protection: point cost - protected cost, split into bias (point - bias-corrected) and margin (bias-corrected - protected)
saving against the protected plans of Seasonal naive and of Persistence: baseline cost - plan cost
share of avoidable cost removed: (baseline cost - plan cost) / (baseline cost - hindsight cost), same baselines
skill against Seasonal naive: 1 - loss / Seasonal naive loss, for pinball loss at 0.9 and for gap MAE
excess over hindsight, in model units and as a percentage of hindsight cost
per origin and combined; combined ratios are ratios of sums
rules.indicative: the 0.95 level (p = 10,000 and alpha = 0.05) is the largest past error and is indicative only

disclosures: the outcome months, the bias of each method in each window, the Persistence result at March 2026 and the earlier SARIMA SAA result were known before this design was written; the rules are fixed in advance but not blind
error paths overlap: 29 and 35 paths carry the information of about 5 and 6 independent six-month blocks
the 0.95 level (p = 10,000 and alpha = 0.05) is the largest past error and is indicative only
the gap is measured against 90% occupancy, itself a safety ceiling; a shortfall means occupancy above 90%
all six months are fixed at the origin; there is no re-planning
NHS revised Sep 2026 between the September and October 2026 publications (available -87, occupied -2); the October 2026 publication is used throughout
SARIMA-24 and ExtraTrees-24 are the small-sample variants of the clean checkpoint
costs are illustrative model units (validated: False)
procedure: write and hash this config before any backtest or forecast
plan stage: data up to each origin only; backtests, scenarios and all plans for both origins; hash them
score stage: verify both hashes, load the target months, solve hindsight, score once, apply the rules
